λ-RMSD along the 18-conformer Ag complex ensemble, with and without hydrogens, and a check of what
the method cannot see (enantiomers).

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/ensemble.xyz` — 18 conformers of an Ag complex, 168 atoms
* `files/nmr_iPr.xyz` — organic molecule with two stereocentres, 39 atoms

**1. Every conformer against the first one** (all atoms).

```bash
frog-rmsd files/ensemble.xyz
```


Conformer 0 is the reference (0.000). Conformers 4 (0.504 Å) and 11 (0.611 Å) are the closest to it,
conformers 15 (5.051 Å) and 16 (4.823 Å) the most different. Both belong to the family with a
positive P50–Ag0–C4–N3 dihedral (see the `frog-internals` and `frog-sort` examples), unlike
conformer 0.

**2. Heavy atoms only**, as CSV.

```bash
frog-rmsd files/ensemble.xyz --no-hydrogen --format csv -q
```

Without hydrogens all values are smaller (e.g. conformer 15: 3.067 Å instead of 5.051 Å), because the
H atoms are left out of the distance matrix. The ranking is almost the same. Compare values only
within one setting, never with and without `--no-hydrogen`.

**3. Enantiomers.** `files/nmr_iPr_mirror.xyz` is the mirror image of `files/nmr_iPr.xyz`
(written by `frog-mirror` in a hidden step).

```bash
frog-rmsd files/nmr_iPr_mirror.xyz -r files/nmr_iPr.xyz
```

```text
ℹ  Processing files/nmr_iPr_mirror.xyz
      λ-RMSD (reference: files/nmr_iPr.xyz)
╭───────────────────────────────────┬────────────╮
│ Structure                         │ λ-RMSD (Å) │
├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────┤
│ files/nmr_iPr_mirror.xyz - Conf 0 │      0.000 │
╰───────────────────────────────────┴────────────╯
```

The two enantiomers give exactly 0.000: reflection does not change any distance. Use
`frog-stereocenters` to tell enantiomers apart.
